parties:
Ibn Sina Trust ------ Petitioner 
Vs 
Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd and anr ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Arayesuddin J: This Rule was issued calling upon opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 1-4-2004 by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 105 of 2004 rejecting an application under Order XXI, rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceedings of Money Execution Case No. 89 of 2003 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, Court, No. 3 Dhaka regarding auction sale of the petitioner's property till disposal of Title Suit No. 105 of 2004 should not be set aside. 

 2. Relevant fact to dispose of the Rule, in brief, is that the petitioner is a Charitable Organisation registered under the Societies Act, 1982 having good reputation and countrywide name and fame. The petitioner organisation claims to be the lawful owner of the suit property. They did not take any loan from the opposite party Bank. They are not also a guarantor for the money borrowed from the Bank. Yet the opposite party Bank obtained a decree for realisation of the loan money, availed and enjoyed by the opposite party No. 2. In the impugned suit petitioner was imploaded as defendant No. 4. The summons and notice were suppressed and playing fraud upon the Court as well as the parties plaintiff-opposite party No.1 obtained the impugned judgment and decree. Petitioner had no relief under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure as they are not third party. No relief can also be claimed by filing Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code since the suit has been dismissed ex-parte against the petitioner. Therefore, the petitioner was compelled to file a separate suit being Title Suit No. 105 of 2004 in the Court of the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka challenging the fraudulent decree in view of the decision passed in CPLA No. 572 of 1994 reported in 1995 BLD (AD) 35. In this suit petitioner filed a petition under Order XXI, rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for stay of all further proceeding of the Artha Jari Case No. 89 of 2003 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 3. Dhaka regarding the auction sale of the petitioner's property till disposal of Title Suit No. 105 of 2004 which was rejected by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka on 1-4-2004 in Title Suit No. 105 of 2004. Being aggrieved, petitioner moved this Court in revisional Jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. 

 4. On behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner, the learned Advocate Mr Enayet Hossain Khan submitted the petitioner is a reputed welfare trust extending medical help to the general public throughout the country and they had no need of money to solicit any loan from the Bank. The petitioner purchased the suit land in 1986. At the time of purchase their vendor did not supply the original deed on the plea that it was lost. The petitioner believed the vendor. Petitioner is in possession of the suit land. But subsequently, their vendor, by suppressing the fact of the alleged transfer took loan from the bank by mortgaging the suit property on deposit of the 'title deed. The Bank, without making any further enquiry about the title and possession, allowed the loan by keeping the original deed. The vendor became a defaulter. As a result Bank filed Title Suit No. 116 of 1998 for realisation of the loan money. In the suit petitioner was made defendant No. 4. But the Bank in collusion with the borrower suppressed all the summons and notices and obtained ex-parte decree against this petitioner. But contested decree was passed against the borrower. The Bank put the decree in execution by filing Money Execution Case No. 89 of 2003. In the judgment the trial Court observed that the borrower has no title in the other lands. So, the land possessed by the petitioner measuring 17 decimals has been put to auction. At the time the petitioner came to know of the impugned judgment and decree. In the meantime the perfod of limitation for filing Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was over. He submitted that finding no other alternative petitioner instituted a separate suit as per decision of the Appellate Division and filed a petition under Order XXI, rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying the further proceeding of the Money Execution Case No. 89 of 2003. The learned trial Court without considering the petition on merit rejected the same which is not tenable in law. He has further submitted that the trial Court ought to have passed the order of stay till disposal of the suit. To strengthen his argument the learned Advocate submitted that if the suit of the petitioner is decreed and in the meantime he is dispossessed from the suit land there would be further litigation and the very purpose of the suit will be frustrated. The learned Advocate submitted that honorable Appellate Division has categorically opined that the allegation of non-service of summons in a suit of Artha Rin Adalat can be challenged by filing separate suit. 

 5. On behalf of the opposite party No.1, Mr Morshed Ahmed Khan, the learned Advocate submitted that there is no illegality in the impugned order complained of. He has submitted that petitioner wilfully did not contest the suit. He had sufficient relief in the suit of the Artha Rin Adalat. To elucidate his argument the learned Advocate submitted that the suit has been decreed ex parte against him. So, the proper forum for the petitioner was to file a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure which is not barred till today if he can prove that he was not aware of the impugned judgment and decree and he acquired knowledge on a certain date. He has further submitted that provision of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable in the case of Artha Rin Adalat if it is not contrary to the provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Further submitted, that in section 57, Artha Rin Adalat has been vested with inherent power to grant any relief to the aggrieved party. The learned Advocate submitted that there were sufficient forums before the petitioner to have his remedies in the Artha Rin Adalat, instead of that he has filed a separate suit and prayed for stay of the execution case in that suit. He has submitted that both the courts are of equal power and jurisdiction. In such circumstances the court of the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka had nothing to do with the execution case of the Artha Rin Adalat which has been established by a separate statute. The learned Advocate for the opposite party No.1 submitted that there is no merit in the Rule as there are forums still today open before the petitioner in the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 6. We have perused the petition, the Rule and the counter-affidavit and heard the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides. It is admitted that the petitioner was defendant No. 4 in Title Suit No. 116 of 1998. Petitioner's contention is that he did not receive any summons and notices of that suit. So he could not contest. His further allegation is that plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 collusively suppressed the summons by practicing fraud upon the court. We have perused the judgment of our honorable Appellate Division delivered in CPLA No. 572 of 1994 in the case of Md Mozammel Hoque vs Sonali Bank and another. In that judgment the Appellate Division has given the exhaustive guideline in para 3 which runs as follows: 

 3. "In the facts and circumstances of the case, if the petitioner's allegation of no service of summons of the suit is correct his remedy of a separate suit is not barred provided his remedy lies under the Artha Rin Adalat Act stood barred at the time of the filing of the suit for no fault of his own. But these are matters of evidence and until the plaintiff petitioner proves these allegations in the suit the decree holder respondent Bank cannot be denied the fruit of its decree for an indefinite period." 

 With this exhaustive findings their Lordships of the Appellate Division was pleased to dismiss the petition for leave to appeal. In the above findings a clear guideline has been given. A separate suit is not barred provided his remedies under the Artha Rin Adalat Act stood barred at the time of filing of the suit for no fault of his own. Annexure A is the judgment of Title Suit No. 116 of 1998. The suit has been decreed in preliminary form against defendant Nos. 1-2 and 3 and dismissed ex-parte against defendant Nos. 3-4. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that he cannot claim any relief before the Artha Rin Adalat. We are unable to accept this submission in view of the application of the Code of Civil Procedure in the Artha Rin Adalat, Act, 1990 under which the suit Was filed. Section 5(4) of the Act is clear to the effect. Therefore, we find that the door of the Code of Civil Procedure is still' open to the petitioner if he can prove that no summons of notices were served upon him and he had no knowledge of the suit. The learned Advocate submitted that petitioner has no scope to file Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the suit has been dismissed ex parte against him. The definition of decree has been misconceived. The leaned Advocate for opposite party No. 1 also admits that petitioner can seek his relief under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure if he can over come limitation.
